html:
A Vietnamese scholar, official and poet of the 16th century, remembered above all for his prophecies, which rival lords sought in Vietnam's age of division.

He came first in the court exams in 1535 under the Mạc dynasty, which had seized the throne from the Lê. He served the Mạc for some years, then retired to teach after the court ignored his call to punish corrupt officials. He took the title Trình Quốc công and is known as Trạng Trình.

These were the years when the country split between the Mạc in the north and the Lê restored by the Trịnh and Nguyễn families. All sides asked his advice. The best known story is that he told Nguyễn Hoàng that the Hoành Sơn mountains could shelter a family for ten thousand generations. Nguyễn Hoàng then took a post in the far south, and his family became the Nguyễn lords who ruled the south for two centuries. His poems are classics, and the Cao Đài religion counts him as a saint.
sum: A Vietnamese scholar, official and poet of the 16th century, remembered above all for his prophecies, which rival lords sought in Vietnam's age of division.
